name: Catecholaminergic Polymorphic Ventricular Tachycardia

criteria.description: Bidirectional or polymorphic ventricular tachycardia induced by exercise or emotional stress
Normal resting 12-lead ECG without QT prolongation
Pathogenic mutation in RYR2 or CASQ2 gene
Family history of sudden cardiac death or exercise-induced syncope

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of exercise or stress-induced bidirectional or polymorphic ventricular tachycardia with normal resting ECG, with or without a pathogenic mutation in RYR2 or CASQ2 genes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires exercise stress testing or catecholamine challenge to provoke arrhythmia.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic arrhythmia pattern on stress testing
searchTerms: bidirectional fast heart rate during exercise

pathognomonic.symptomName: Polymorphic ventricular tachycardia triggered by emotional stress
searchTerms: emotional stress causes fast heart rhythm

common.notes: No QT prolongation or structural abnormalities

rare.symptomName: Seizure-like activity secondary to cerebral hypoperfusion
searchTerms: seizure-like episodes from low brain blood flow

rare.symptomName: Sudden infant death syndrome in affected families

imaging: Normal echocardiogram without structural heart disease
Exercise stress test showing bidirectional or polymorphic VT
genetic: Pathogenic variants in RYR2 gene (autosomal dominant)
Pathogenic variants in CASQ2 gene (autosomal recessive)
other: Normal resting ECG with no QT prolongation

distinguishingFeatures: Prolonged QT interval on resting ECG
Torsades de pointes rather than bidirectional VT
Fibrofatty replacement of right ventricular myocardium

redFlags: Syncope during exercise or emotional stress
Family history of sudden cardiac death at young age
Exercise-induced polymorphic or bidirectional ventricular tachycardia
references: Priori SG, et al. 2013 HRS/EHRA/APHRS expert consensus statement on the diagnosis and management of patients with inherited primary arrhythmia syndromes. Heart Rhythm. 2013.
Leenhardt A, et al. Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia in children. Circulation. 1995.
Hayashi M, et al. Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia. Circ Arrhythm Electrophysiol. 2009.
